about: Shared test data for the NPU queue (NPU-QUEUE.md, beside this file). Its home is the Steward's kit, the spec part (kit/spec); it was Reeve's. Every implementation (the kit's core, which its node and dotnet parts run, Reeve's src/npu-queue.ts until it takes the kit, and npu-embed's npu_lock.py) must order these tickets (order), judge these heartbeats (dead) and lock holders (holders: owner says whether owner.json reads as {pid, since}; sinceAgeMs is now less its since, folderAgeMs now less the lock folder's modification time, null when it is gone; staleMs, when given, the caller's limit, else 10 minutes) and name these folders (slots) exactly as listed. Keys a reader doesn't know are for others: skip them. The timings are rules.json's, beside this file. Take this file from a kit release, unchanged.

order.case: one lane is first come, first served
a person waiting goes ahead of background work that came first
background work waiting 120 s or more counts as interactive, so it is served by arrival
same lane and time: lower pid first, then the nonce
anything that isn't a ticket is ignored

dead.case: fresh heartbeat, process gone: not dead yet
late heartbeat, process alive: still waiting
exactly 5 s late is not late
no heartbeat for over 15 s: dead even if the pid is alive (pids get reused)
exactly 15 s is not dead while the process is alive

slots.case: the NPU: one slot, its folder as always
the second card of a name

holders.case: a live holder within its 10 minutes keeps the lock
a holder whose process is gone is evicted
a holder over 10 minutes is evicted, whatever its pid says
a caller's longer limit keeps an older holder
no owner.json and the folder 2 s old: a holder about to write it
no owner.json for over 10 s: a crash leftover
no owner.json, the folder exactly 10 s old: not yet
no owner.json and the folder gone: nothing to evict
